about.title: Truckee Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Truckee's mix of mountain highways and seasonal traffic creates unique challenges after a crash. Nevada County recorded 54 injury collisions and 73 people injured in the most recent year, with reports clustering on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. — often along Donner Pass Road, I-80, and Route 267. Snow, tourist congestion, and steep grades can complicate how a collision happens and how insurers try to assign blame afterward. LawProactive isn't a law firm; we're a free service that connects injured Truckee residents and visitors with an independent personal injury attorney familiar with California's rules on fault and evidence. Early steps matter — skid patterns, dashcam footage, and witness accounts near these corridors can fade or disappear quickly, especially with fast-changing mountain weather. Getting matched with an attorney soon after a crash can help make sure your side of the story is documented and protected before the insurance company gets to shape the narrative first.

whyChoose.title: Why Truckee Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Time Limits Apply Fast
items.desc: California generally gives you two years to file a car accident claim, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity (like a road maintenance agency) may be responsible. Connecting with an attorney early helps make sure you don't miss a deadline.

items.title: Comparative Fault Means Every Detail Counts
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly blamed for a Donner Pass Road or I-80 collision, you can still pursue compensation reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help make sure fault isn't overstated against you.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering, But Protect Your Words First
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, but insurers often ask for recorded statements to use against you later. It's wise to speak with an attorney before giving one, and there's no fee unless you recover.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim after a crash in Truckee?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. That window can be much shorter — sometimes six months — if a government agency, such as one responsible for road conditions on a highway like I-80, may share fault. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies to your situation.

items.question: Will winter weather or road conditions affect my claim if I was hurt near Donner Pass Road?
items.answer: Weather and road conditions can be part of the evidence in a crash claim, but they don't automatically decide fault. What matters is how the facts are documented — skid marks, visibility, maintenance records — before that evidence disappears with the next storm. An independent attorney can help gather and preserve that information.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters often use those statements to shift blame or minimize your claim. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney who can advise you on what to say and when.
